page.title: A season of selling the seat
page.description: One Islanders season at UBS Arena, Schaefer surge to renewal. Public facts cited; ticketing, CRM, app, scanning and POS flows are illustrative, not any team's or vendor's systems.

sections.heading: The Schaefer effect
text: How a team sells, fills and follows up on a season of seats at UBS Arena, from the 2025 Schaefer demand surge to next year's renewal, told with the New York Islanders' public promotions. Public facts are cited on each step (open the green markers); the ticketing, CRM, app, scanning and POS flows are illustrative reconstructions, not any team's or vendor's systems, and figures are illustrative unless a source is given.
bullets: The **fact tiles** light one at a time, each with its date; dimmed tiles have no claim yet
The **300 level** fills section by section as each fact lands (illustrative): sidelines first, then corners, then the far ends
The **crowd tiles** track the illustrative crowd against about 17,250 seats

**Season at a glance:** Jun 27, 2025 the No. 1 pick (this section) · Jul 24, 2026 single-game on-sale (5) · Aug 25 promo schedule (2, 3) · Oct 22 a friend's ticket (13) · Nov 7 hat night (10, 11) · Nov 27 Sorokin night (9) · Dec 1 GOAT USA Night (12) · Feb 13, 2027 Schaefer bobblehead (3) · Mar 27 Greek Heritage Night (7) · renewal and All-Star 2027 (14)

sections.heading: The 120-day bobblehead clock
text: An all-fans bobblehead night is a supply chain with a fixed end date. Working back from Sat Feb 13, 2027, four lanes run in parallel: sponsor and licensing approvals, production, freight, and event ops. Each lane has a *last safe change* date, after which a change costs the night.

The lanes table shows each lane's *last safe change* and its status; the checks show each gate; the budget shows the 172 days from announcement to game night running out and the schedule slack being spent. Pick a path to see freight arrive or slip.
bullets: **Public facts:** the Schaefer bobblehead for all fans on Feb 13 vs MIN, presented by Northwell ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/new-york-islanders-promotional-giveaways-include-schaefer-sorokin-bobbleheads-exclusive-home-opener-t-shirt)); about 120 days to manufacture ([MASN](https://masnsports.com/blog/behind-the-scenes-of-the-bobblehead-giveaway)); a late delivery (Yankees, [NPR](https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2013/09/25/226071535/yankees-bobble-the-ball-on-mariano-rivera-give-away-night)); digital vouchers (Pirates, [CBS Pittsburgh](https://www.cbsnews.com/pittsburgh/news/the-pirates-are-giving-paul-skenes-bobblehead-vouchers)).
**Illustrative:** every date after Aug 25, the 18,000 quantity, case counts, transit time, slack and the redemption window. No Islanders vendor, freight or ops detail is claimed.
**The lesson:** the approval lane spends slack first, and the voucher plan is cheapest when it is written before T-30.

sections.heading: Holds that quietly expire
text: A group hold takes seats off sale before anyone has paid for them. It is borrowed inventory with an expiry date, and on that date it either converts to sold or goes back on sale. This section follows three holds on one game and forks at the final-payment date.

Section numbering is from public seating guides; capacities are an illustrative even split of 17,250 seats over 80 sections. The groups, deposits, sales and prices are illustrative. The group bar near Sec 210 is a [sourced 2026-27 announcement](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/islanders-unveil-new-fan-experiences-ahead-of-2026-27-season-x1088). The ticketing, CRM and reporting flow is an illustrative reconstruction, not any team's or vendor's system.
bullets: Hatched sections are held: they count against capacity but not against sold
Choose **Converts** or **Expires silently** below the step controls; both paths share the first six steps

steps.deltaText: Deposit models are published group policies of other clubs: a $200 non-refundable deposit to hold a date (an older Cleveland Guardians group-policy page) and a 20% deposit with full payment 45 days out (Atlanta Braves). The amounts in this table are illustrative.

The school's is **pending** on a district PO.

steps.text: Each night pricing pulls a **snapshot** of holds. Held seats look committed, so the upper-deck offer skips 312–314 and 320–321.
**T-7d, final payment.** The youth club and the corporate outing pay in full and turn sold. The school hold is left: pick **Converts** or **Expires silently**.
The district's PO clears that afternoon. Group sales converts the hold before midnight: **600 seats in 312–314 turn sold** and no hatches remain.
Ticketing **bulk-transfers** the 600 tickets to the leader's app account. The leader forwards them to families; any not forwarded by doors become a gate line.

holds.note: Delivery is a bulk transfer to each group's leader.

steps.text: Recap. Tonight's snapshot matches ticketing: **0 held**, and 312–314 show full on the sold map because every group seat is now paid revenue. When holds convert, a stale report does no harm.
Midnight passes unpaid. Ticketing **releases the hold on its own**: the hatch clears and 600 seats go back on sale. No notice reaches group sales or pricing.

holds.note: The school hold expired. Nobody was told.

steps.text: Pricing's report still shows the 600 as **held**. To the desk 312–314 is full, so the offer goes out **without** the 630 seats that are actually open.
Game night: 312–314 was never offered and draws only walk-ups. The fix is process, not price: **a hold expiry should be an event** that alerts sales, pricing and marketing.

sections.heading: On-sale day: 4,812th in line
text: On a big on-sale, the first problem is traffic, not sales. A waiting room holds thousands of fans and lets them into seat select in batches; when one fan finally gets through, the best seats may already be gone to the presale, and the pair they tap can vanish into someone else's cart.

Facts with a source link: the July 24, 2026 noon on-sale with a priority presale ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/islanders-announce-2026-27-regular-season-schedule)), how Ticketmaster describes its waiting room ([Smart Queue](https://business.ticketmaster.com/smart-queue/)), and the FTC all-in fee rule effective May 12, 2025 ([GRC Report](https://www.grcreport.com/post/ftc-rule-on-unfair-or-deceptive-fees-to-take-effect-on-may-12-2025)). The fan's position, wait times, prices, cart timer and sell-through are illustrative. Seat-map capacities are an illustrative even split of 17,250 seats over 80 sections.
bullets: **Queue** is the hero: one fan joins the waiting room, gets place **4,812** at noon, is let through to seat select, then is held again as two seats in a cart until payment

sections.heading: The pace curve and the member floor
text: A week out, the 300 level is behind pace while the lower bowl runs hot. A price cut can fill it, but only if it does not undercut the season members who paid for those seats in advance, and only if every channel shows the new price. This section walks one game on the UBS Arena map from T-30 to the revenue recap.

Public facts are cited from press and league sources. Ticketing, CRM, app and ad flows are illustrative reconstructions of common industry practice, not descriptions of any team's or vendor's systems. Prices, sales, the pace target and the $31 member per-game price are illustrative; capacities are an even split of 17,250 seats over 80 sections, not venue data. Whether UBS Arena prices dynamically is not verified: this is a generic method on an Islanders-shaped map.
bullets: **Dynamic pricing is not new in hockey.** The SF Giants piloted it with Qcue in 2009, and the Dallas Stars were the first NHL club to follow the same year ([Qcue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qcue), [Sports Illustrated](https://vault.si.com/vault/2009/02/23/tickets-with-flex), [ODU](https://www.odu.edu/news/news-archive/2011/05/ODUProfS_27566)).

**Prices move inside guardrails.** On Ticketmaster, Official Platinum prices are set by the event organizer, such as the team ([Ticketmaster](https://help.ticketmaster.com/hc/en-us/articles/9782440112017-What-are-Official-Platinum-Seats)); the floor and ceiling used here are the author's illustration; the Bruins' flex pricing varies per-game prices for plan holders ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/bruins/tickets/flex-pricing)).

**The member floor** is the guardrail that matters most here: a public seat cheaper than a member's per-game price teaches fans to wait. A fan newsletter made that argument about cheap late tickets in 2024; it is opinion, not data ([Isles Fix](https://www.islesfix.com/p/taking-attendance)).

**All-in prices.** Since May 12, 2025 the FTC fee rule requires the first price shown to include mandatory fees ([GRC Report](https://www.grcreport.com/post/ftc-rule-on-unfair-or-deceptive-fees-to-take-effect-on-may-12-2025)).
Choose **Hold at $38** or **Drop to member floor** below the step controls. Both end on the sold map, with the 300-level revenue in the tiles.

steps.text: The pricing desk proposes cutting the 300 level from **$38 to $29**. Before it ships, the guardrails run. The CRM returns the member per-game price for the same seats: **$31** (illustrative). The proposal **fails**: a public $29 seat would undercut the season member sitting next to it.

**Recap, held price.** The map stays on sold: the 300 level ends at 41% while the lower bowl carries the night. The tile shows what the upper ring earns: about **$87.7k**. **Recap, member floor.** The map stays on sold: the 300 level ends at 72%. The tile shows about **$125k** against $87.7k on the held path. sections.heading: Two hundred fifty shirts, one link
text: A heritage night looks like a theme on the scoreboard. Underneath, it is a **separate ticket product** with its own link, its own capped item stock and a redemption list tied to barcodes. The Islanders' 2026-27 schedule lists Greek Heritage Night on **Mar 27, 2027 vs Detroit**, with a Greek T-shirt for the *first 250 buyers* ([schedule](https://nhl.com/islanders/tickets/promotional-schedule)). The same pattern ran at the 2024-25 Pride Night on Jan 16, 2025: a belt bag for the first 500 special-ticket buyers ([The Hockey News](https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-york-islanders/players/new-york-islanders-promo-nights-group-nights-ubs-arena-release)).
The partner names, codes, clicks, sales and new-to-file counts below are **illustrative**, as are the offer page, CRM and redemption flows. Pick a path to see the shirts sell out or fall short.

bullets.text: **Unique codes per partner** show which community actually brings in *new* fans, not only sales.
**Tie the item count to sales.** Each special-offer ticket reserves one shirt, so the cap is enforced by the sale itself.
**Plan both endings:** offer copy that flips when the item is gone, and a home for leftovers.

sections.heading: The buyer is not the attendee
text: Entry at UBS Arena is mobile only, and each barcode appears in the app 48 hours before puck drop ([Islanders mobile tickets](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/tickets/mobile-tickets-troubleshooting)). Primary tickets are sold through Ticketmaster ([Islanders tickets](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/tickets/islanders-tickets)). After that, a ticket can stay with its buyer, move to a friend, or be resold, and each route leaves a different trail in the team's data.

Follow seat 6 of a two-seat order through each route: the ticket's lifecycle, the buyer's phone, the CRM record and the feeds each route lights. Dana R. and Sam K. are fictional, and the systems, feeds and figures are illustrative reconstructions of common practice, not any team's or vendor's internals.

bullets.text: **The lesson:** the *scan list*, not the order list, says who was in the building.
**Why it matters:** giveaway counts, recap emails, loyalty points and churn signals all change with it.
**The opportunity:** transfer recipients have attended but never bought, so they are warm first-purchase prospects.

sections.heading: Ten thousand hats, six doors
text: On a *first 10,000* night the count is never only total supply. It is ten thousand hats split across six doors, drawn down at different speeds by a Park crowd at one entrance and a train at another. The Islanders gave camo hats to the first 10,000 on Military Appreciation nights in [2024](https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-york-islanders/players/new-york-islanders-promo-nights-group-nights-ubs-arena-release) and [2025](https://www.amny.com/sports/islanders-giveaways-25-26-8-19-25); on **Nov 7, 2026 vs New Jersey** it is a Ford camo hat ([schedule](https://nhl.com/islanders/tickets/promotional-schedule)).

Each bar counts **claims on one gate's stock**: hats handed out there, cases sent to another gate, and first-10,000 fans turned away. NEAR, AT and OVER LIMIT are the ops desk's cues. Names, dates, The Park on the Plaza, the AmEx and NE entrances and the LIRR station are public facts. Gates C to F, every split, count, case size and time are illustrative, and the scan, inventory and radio flow is a reconstruction of common practice, not any team's or vendor's system.
bullets: **Fork at T-45:** choose *Move cases* or *No action* below the step controls. Both end with every gate out and the last hat logged
**The difference is who got the hat,** not how many: the sponsor recap reads 10,000 either way
**Operator fix:** put a live per-gate count against allotment in front of the ops desk

bullets: Chick-fil-A's Score First promotion at UBS Arena is real and cited; the game, times, counts and contracted assets are illustrative.
Pick a path: if the Islanders score first the chain runs for two days; if the opponent does, it stays idle.
Either way the night ends with a sponsor recap: what was delivered, what was made good, and what the team cannot see.

steps.text: **Before puck drop.** Chick-fil-A's *Score First* promotion is real: when the Islanders score first in a regular-season home game at UBS Arena, Chick-fil-A One app users can claim a free reward the next day, at participating Tri-State restaurants, one per account, no purchase needed. Take a Saturday night home game, Nov 7, 2026 vs New Jersey (7 p.m. on the schedule). The game below is made up; the sponsor assets on the checklist are illustrative.

chk.note: Seven contracted items for tonight (illustrative). Nothing delivered yet.

fun.note: Nothing to count until something happens on the ice.

steps.text: **Puck drop.** The game clock starts and so do the assets that run whatever the score: the LED ribbon rotates in its slots and the P1 PA read airs at the first TV timeout. The trigger lanes sit idle. Nothing in the chain can fire until the first goal, and only the first goal counts.

**8:14 of P1: the Islanders score first** (illustrative). The official event feed records the goal, and that one data point is the trigger. Game presentation gets the cue: the goal horn, then the Score First graphic on the board and a PA line telling fans to open the sponsor app on Monday.

chk.note: Trigger met. The board graphic is now delivered.

fun.note: Reach starts with the fans in the bowl: 14,900 scanned (illustrative).

steps.text: **The chain fans out.** The feed's job is done once the goal is official. Team social posts the trigger ("Isles scored first, claim Monday"), and the post keeps collecting reach long after the cue on the board is gone. The reward itself is not live yet: the next lane to open is the sponsor's, two days from now.

fun.note: Arena plus social impressions, and clicks and shares on the post (illustrative).

steps.text: **Tied after 60 minutes, so overtime.** The run of show switches to its overtime script and the sponsor read slotted for the last P3 TV timeout is cut. That is a contracted asset not delivered: the checklist shows it amber, and the activation manager books a make-good read for the next home game. Losing in OT changes nothing for fans: the trigger was the first goal.

pa3.detail: cut: overtime script took the slot

makegood.detail: extra PA read added to the next home game

chk.note: One miss, one make-good. Proof is a log, not a memory.

steps.text: **Final horn after overtime.** The game lane and the in-game asset log close together: everything the contract promised inside the arena has now run, been cut and made good, or been correctly skipped. Whether anything happens after tonight depends only on who scored first.

**Sunday: the gap.** The post has done most of its work, and nothing can be claimed. Participating restaurants are closed on Sundays, which is why a Saturday trigger is claimed on Monday. The step axis shows it plainly: the event happened two lanes and a full day before the reward exists.

fun.note: Team-side numbers are final: 182,000 reached, 7,400 engaged (illustrative).

steps.text: **Monday: the sponsor's app unlocks the reward** and fans redeem at participating Tri-State restaurants. Both lanes run on the sponsor's systems, so the team sees the bars open but none of the counts: claims and redemptions sit in the sponsor's app and POS.

fun.note: Claims and redemptions: sponsor-held: not shared with the team (illustrative contract).

steps.text: **The recap for the sponsor.** The team can prove four in-game assets, plus the cut P3 read and its make-good, and it can report reach and engagement. It cannot report claims or redemptions, because the contract never asked for them. The fix is a contract line, not a dashboard: claim counts by game, shared within a week.

makegood.detail: extra PA read added to the next home game

data.detail: not in the contract: no claim data

chk.note: Delivered and proven: 5 passes, 1 warn with make-good. Attribution: missing.

fun.note: Reach and engagement are the team's. Claims and redemptions stay with the sponsor.

steps.text: **6:02 of P1: New Jersey scores first** (illustrative). The event feed records a first goal, but the wrong team's, so the trigger condition fails for the whole night. No cue goes to the board, no post is queued and no unlock is scheduled.

chk.note: Trigger-only assets skip; they are not misses.

fun.note: No reward tonight: nothing to count.

steps.text: **The Isles equalize in P2, and it does not matter.** The promotion keys on the first goal only. The horn and goal song run as normal, but the Score First lanes stay idle. This is the budget side of a trigger promo: its cost, and its reach, rise and fall with how often the team scores first.

fun.note: No reward tonight: no post, so no Score First reach.

steps.text: **Tied after 60 minutes, so overtime.** The run of show switches to its overtime script and the sponsor read slotted for the last P3 TV timeout is cut. Contracted assets are owed whatever the score: the read turns amber and a make-good is booked for the next home game.

chk.note: Same miss as any OT night, same make-good.

steps.text: **Final horn after overtime.** The game lane and the in-game asset log close together: everything the contract promised inside the arena has now run, been cut and made good, or been correctly skipped. Whether anything happens after tonight depends only on who scored first.

**Sunday, then Monday.** The sponsor's lanes never open: no unlock, no restaurant traffic. The funnel's last stages still read sponsor-held, a reminder that even on a night it fires, the team would not see the claims.

fun.note: No reward tonight. On a trigger night these stages would still be sponsor-held: not shared.

steps.text: **The recap for the sponsor, on a night without a trigger.** The proof is shorter but still owed: three assets delivered, one cut and made good, two correctly skipped. The open question is the same as on a trigger night: claim data is not in the contract.

text: A trigger promotion turns one moment of the game into a sponsor's marketing event. When the Islanders score first at a regular-season home game, Chick-fil-A's Score First promotion unlocks a free reward in the sponsor's app the next day: the team runs the cue in the building, and the sponsor runs the reward.

sections.heading: The morning after
text: The final horn is not the end of the night's marketing. By 8 a.m. the fan's phone holds the team's recap, a sponsor's reward and a partner's offer, and two rules decide whether any of it works: **send to the people who came**, and **match the tone to the score**.

Public facts (the Dec 1, 2026 GOAT USA Night, Chick-fil-A Score First, the Belmont Park offer, mobile-only entry) are cited on the steps that use them. The CRM, scan, ticketing and email flows are illustrative reconstructions of common practice, not any team's or vendor's systems. The game result, send times, message wording and every count are illustrative.
bullets: **Scan list, not order list:** the recap audience is who walked in, including friends on transferred tickets.
**Tone follows the result:** highlight-led after a win, next-game-led after a loss.
**The stack is a budget:** three cards show; the fourth becomes *+1 more*.

sections.heading: Clinch or fade
text: In mid-March nobody knows whether the playoff games exist, yet members must be invoiced, presales staged and giveaways sourced. Playoff ticketing is **conditional inventory**: it is built and priced before the schedule is real, and the elimination branch needs as much planning as the clinch.

Two paths share one board. **Eliminated** is what actually happened to the 2025-26 Islanders (out on Apr 12, 2026). **Clinch** replays the April 2024 playbook (home Games 3 and 4 against Carolina). Both end at the 2026-27 renewal, where All-Star 2027 priority is the lever.
bullets: **Sourced:** 2024 Round 1 dates and Apr 20 on-sale ([NHL.com](https://nhl.com/islanders/news/islanders-hurricanes-first-round-schedule-announced-2024)); rally towels, commemorative ticket and doors 90 minutes early ([The Hockey News](https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-york-islanders/game-day/new-york-islanders-playoffs-ubs-arena-hurricanes-game-three)); elimination Apr 12, 2026 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_New_York_Islanders_season)); All-Star 2027 member priority and waitlist ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/fans/all-star)); $100 membership deposit, published for 2025-26 ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/tickets/2025-26-deposits)).
**Pattern, not Islanders policy:** charge at clinch or on a date, and credits for unplayed games, follow the [Oilers' 2026 FAQ](https://www.nhl.com/oilers/tickets/season-seat-holders/renewal-faq).
**Illustrative:** member accounts, prices, risk reasons, the All-Star allocation split, every funnel count and all sell-through. Seat capacities are an even split of 17,250 over 80 sections.

steps.text: **Mid-March 2026: in the hunt.** The standings move nightly, so ticket ops builds playoff inventory for home games that may never exist. Every section is *held* for a conditional Round 1 home game, and nothing is on sale yet.

steps.text: **Pre-build both branches.** Member playoff invoices are queued to charge *at clinch or on a fixed date, whichever comes first* (the Oilers published this rule for 2026). Marketing drafts the presale email *and* the credit email, and promotions gets a rally-towel quote, because towels can be made in days and bobbleheads cannot.

steps.text: **Clinch (the branch that did not happen in 2026).** The magic number hits zero. Billing charges the first home game, and the schedule fixes the dates. The playbook is April 2024: Round 1 against Carolina, home Games 3 and 4 at UBS Arena on Apr 25 and 27.

steps.text: **Game night.** Every seat is sold and every seat gets a rally towel. This is the 2024 precedent: towels and a commemorative ticket for all fans, The Park with contests, doors 90 minutes early. Game 4 went to double overtime and the Islanders won 3-2.

steps.text: **The date trigger fires first.** No clinch yet, but the fixed charge date arrives, so the first playoff payment is taken anyway. This is the trap the pre-built credit email exists for.

steps.text: **Apr 12, 2026: eliminated.** This is what actually happened: a second straight playoff miss for a 43-34-5 team. The conditional inventory is released and the bowl empties. Not one playoff seat was ever sold. Source: [Wikipedia: 2025-26 Islanders season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_New_York_Islanders_season) · [Yardbarker: Islanders eliminated](https://www.yardbarker.com/nhl/articles/islanders_officially_eliminated_from_2026_stanley_cup_playoff_contention/s1_16958_43721010).

steps.text: **Unplayed games become credits.** Each charged payment turns into an account credit for next season, refundable on request (the Oilers' published pattern). The credit email that was drafted in March goes out the same day. Source: [NHL.com Oilers: renewal and 2026 playoffs FAQ](https://www.nhl.com/oilers/tickets/season-seat-holders/renewal-faq).

steps.text: **The same table becomes the rep queue.** Sorted by churn risk: newer members churn more, and a member who asked for a refund after a losing season is the first call. Flag *transferred* seats before calling, because a member whose family uses the seats is not absent. Source: [Chief Marketer: LA Kings churn modelling](https://www.chiefmarketer.com/la-kings-turn-to-modeling-to-ice-churn/).

steps.text: **Both branches meet at renewal.** The 2026-27 renewal carries one line no rival can match: Full and Half Season Members get *guaranteed access to buy tickets* (subject to availability) for the 2027 All-Star Weekend at UBS Arena. Others joined a waitlist; the team's 2025-26 deposit page asked $100 for priority access to a new membership (the 2026-27 amount is not confirmed).

steps.text: **All-Star 2027 closes the loop.** Feb 5-6, 2027: a 3-on-3 round robin with fan voting. Waitlist fans are offered the seats that remain, and the ones who buy get a membership pitch. The event is a one-time acquisition window, so the last funnel stage is the one that matters next season.
